does: Folds a sheet or a round of dough over itself, from the sides and into a square or a letter, so that it stacks into layers or gains strength, and so that any fat or oil brushed between the layers stays shut in them.
how: Rest the dough first, so that it relaxes and does not spring back.
Stretch or roll it into an even sheet on a lightly oiled or floured surface.
Brush or sprinkle the surface with the fat or the dusting the dish asks for, right to the edges.
Lift one edge and fold it over towards the middle, then bring the opposite edge over it, as when folding a letter. For a square, fold the other sides in as well.
Press the folded shape lightly, turn it, and rest it before it is rolled or stretched again.

cues.text: The layers show along a cut edge as fine, even lines.
The dough is supple and springs back slowly, and tears only when it is pulled hard.

mistakes.mistake: Folding dough that is still tense, which tears and shrinks back.
mistakes.fix: Let it rest until it relaxes.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the corners and edges bare, so that the layers weld together there.
mistakes.fix: Brush the fat right to the edges.

comes_after.why: A dough is rolled or stretched into an even sheet before it is folded.
